answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. In practice this means a farm must spend real resources on every single alias, and that per-identity cost is what keeps the network honest at scale.. This is resilient because unearned rewards are capped and eventually burned, so an attacker cannot bank on a runaway Sybil campaign paying off. Consider a vine as the anchor of the cost.
